payload.title: The object-literal property helpers (isPropertyNamed, readStringProperty and now declaresProperty) are re-declared inside individual adapters, byte-identical in two of them, with no shared owner in adapter-ts.ts
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/event-contracts-adapter.ts:483-491 (the same property-assignment-or-shorthand predicate, used as a count)
tools/aria-adapters/adapter-ts.ts:176-210 (the shared TypeScript owner exports only the contained compiler host and program builder)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner per concept (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2: make the correct behaviour the default); no second copy of one fact
payload.notes: A change to what counts as a property key, for example accepting a computed string key (the gap in the schema-option candidate), has to be made in every copy. The copy that is missed keeps reading the same registry or decorator literal differently from its sibling, so two adapters disagree about one literal with no test coupling them. Close condition: Move isPropertyNamed, readStringProperty and declaresProperty into adapter-ts.ts (or a sibling helper module) and import them in typeorm-entity-schema-adapter.ts and module-schemas-source.ts; closed when a search for 'function isPropertyNamed' under tools/aria-adapters finds exactly one declaration and the adapter tests pass. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
